dog.description_text:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.

Pre-Screener Form

Murphy arrived at MACC as a stray with no known history. While in care, Murphy has been observed to mount handlers frequently. This behavior can be difficult to redirect. Murphy has also been observed to react to the other dogs in the kennel room. In one instance, Murphy nipped a handler on the knee after reacting to a dog. During his previous stay in the care center, Murphy was observed to mount handlers persistently. With handlers Murphy is observed to have a loose body. Due to the detailed behavior we recommend an experienced adult only home.

A Volunteer Wrote: This dog is PERFECTION! Volunteers could not love this dog more for so many reasons! Signage on his kennel warns that he can become overstimulated during walks, but we are guessing that was when he first arrived and was overwhelmedÂ (who wouldn't be?) because he is absolutely glorious company, strolling on a loose leash, completely disinterested in other dogs, but adorably interested in what everyoneÂ around him was doing (playing basketball! Eating picnics!) Murphy watched it all, rolling in the grass before hopping up to sit next to me on a bench. Murphy is a beautiful, young dog who could have the most beautiful, long life ahead of him with you!
dog.name: Murphy
